name: Calendly

identity.note: Calendly API v2. Sandbox and Production OAuth environments exist.

summary: Calendly is a scheduling platform that lets people share booking links and automates meeting scheduling, with a REST API, webhooks, embeds and a hosted MCP server.

auth.detail: OAuth 2.1 (authorization code with PKCE) for public multi-user apps, via an OAuth app created in the developer portal with Sandbox and Production environments. Personal access tokens for internal single-account use.

gates: A few endpoints are Enterprise-only: activity log entries, delete invitee data, delete scheduled event data
Organization-scope webhooks require the user to be an organization admin or owner
The hosted MCP server needs clients that support DCR (dynamic client registration)
Developer-portal docs do not state an app review or marketplace requirement for production OAuth apps; this was not verified

api.note: API v2. The 'other' type is embeds. Resource families were taken from the docs overview and the FAQ, not from the full API reference. The SDK type is not confirmed; the Cursor and CLI repos found are third-party.

mcp.note: Hosted by Calendly. Self-hosting is not supported. Auth is OAuth with DCR. Several community MCP servers also exist.

open_questions: Does a production OAuth app need Calendly review or approval before it can serve many customers? Docs fetched do not say.
Are there rate limits? None were checked.
Is there an official SDK? None was confirmed; only third-party clients were seen.

claims.text: The API v2 supports personal access tokens for internal use and OAuth for public apps.
claims.quote: If you’re integrating a **public application** that many Calendly users will use, authenticate with **OAuth**.

claims.text: API access is available on all subscription plans, including Free, with only a few Enterprise-only endpoints.
claims.quote: Developers can make GET and POST requests to API endpoints on behalf of a Calendly user on any subscription plan, including the Free plan

claims.text: Organization-scoped webhooks need an organization admin or owner. Webhooks are available on all plans.
claims.quote: To create an `organization`-scope webhook subscription, the user must be an organization admin or owner.

claims.text: The REST API covers scheduling, contacts and notetaker data, with webhooks and embeds also available.
claims.quote: Programmatically book meetings and read and write Scheduling, Contacts, and Notetaker data.

claims.text: The official MCP server is hosted by Calendly at mcp.calendly.com.
claims.quote: The server is **fully hosted by Calendly** at `https://mcp.calendly.com`. Self-hosting or local deployment is not supported.

auth.reason: Docs state API v2 uses personal access tokens (internal) and OAuth 2.1 (public apps). Methods oauth2 and personal_token match.

access.reason: FAQ confirms API on any plan including Free, with only three Enterprise-only endpoints and the org-webhook admin requirement. The record correctly flags the unverified app review question.

api.reason: Docs show REST covering Scheduling, Contacts and Notetaker, plus webhooks and embeds. The record honestly notes the SDK is unconfirmed. Listing 'sdk' in types is weakly supported, since only third-party SDKs were seen, so consider removing it.

mcp.reason: Official docs on developer.calendly.com say the MCP server is fully hosted by Calendly at mcp.calendly.com, with DCR OAuth 2.1 and no self-hosting.

verdict.reason: Free-plan API access, OAuth with sandbox, and PATs fit build_now. The Enterprise-only endpoints are a minor carve-out, not a gate on the core API. The unverified public app review would not change the verdict under the rubric. Confidence of medium is reasonable.
